name: Siemens Project File Format
summary: Adversaries may infect Siemens PLC project files (i.e., Step 7, WinCC, etc.) to achieve Execution, Persistence, and Lateral Movement objectives. Adversaries may modify an existing project file or bring their own project files into the environment. The ability for an adversary to deploy an infected project file relies on access to a workstation with Siemens PLC programming software installed on it from which a program download can be performed.

strategies.name: Detection of Siemens Project File Format Infection

analytics.name: Analytic 2049
analytics.guidance: Configured Windows object-access monitoring identifies a write to a Siemens project file by a process that is not the Siemens Totally Integrated Automation (TIA) Portal or Step7 engineering software, or by the legitimate Siemens tool immediately after loading a project from an untrusted path. Directly documented as a Stuxnet mechanism. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. Suppress vendor-signed software, approved engineering utilities, diagnostics, patching, backup, and documented maintenance.…

analytics.name: Analytic 2120
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies a write to a Siemens project file path on a Linux engineering workstation from a User Identifier (UID) not associated with the Siemens engineering tool runtime. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. Suppress vendor-signed software, approved engineering utilities, diagnostics, patching, backup, and documented maintenance.
